report.source_text: Histopathological examination of the sections showed atrophic epidermis with mild hyperkeratosis and flattened rete ridges focally. The underlying papillary was showing a band-like mucin deposit along with focal sclerosis. The middle and deep dermis had patchy mucin along with focal fibrosis. Cuffing of mild to moderate lymphomononuclear infiltrate was observed around perivascular areas in the dermis. Few of the blood vessels were showing endothelial cell proliferation (Figure 2a-c). Scant subcutaneous tissue was available in the biopsy. The result of Alcian blue staining for dermal mucin was positive (Fig. 2d).

clinician.trajectory_summary: A 35-year-old woman presented with painful depigmented porcelain white atrophic papules with surrounding erythema over the trunk, upper limbs, thighs, and chest, associated with mild tenderness. She had a history of joint pain for 7-8 years and recent headache, giddiness, and ocular pain for 3 months. No gastrointestinal symptoms such as abdominal pain or bleeding were reported, only constipation. Physical exam confirmed lesion findings. A skin biopsy revealed epidermal atrophy, mucin deposition, focal sclerosis, lymphomononuclear infiltrate, and endothelial proliferation consistent with Degos disease. Laboratory tests and detailed neurological or joint examinations were not documented. Absence of systemic symptoms and complications led to diagnosis of benign cutaneous Degos disease.
